sop.what: Flags one card used in person in two places that are too far apart to travel between in the time that passed.
sop.brief: One card used in person in two places too far apart for the time between. A physical card cannot be in both. Confirm location with the cardholder. Review surrounding card activity.

sop.what: A rapid burst of small card-not-present authorizations on one card.
sop.why: The detector keys on the burst shape (count, size, gap window), never on a single charge.
sop.brief: A burst of small card-not-present charges in minutes. Criminals test stolen numbers with tiny amounts before spending big. Watch the card for what follows. Confirm the small charges with the cardholder.

sop.what: A run of consecutive magnetic-stripe fallbacks on a chip-capable card.
sop.brief: A run of chip-capable swipes falling back to the magnetic stripe. A cloned stripe cannot complete the chip exchange. Compare the run's locations with the cardholder's. Look for a shared terminal among earlier transactions.

sop.what: One terminal that several cards, later compromised, all used in person shortly before.
sop.why: The detector reads observable compromise signals only (a run of two or more chip-fallback swipes, each within 60 minutes of the last, after the terminal visit).
sop.brief: Several cards that were later compromised all used this one terminal shortly before. A shared terminal is the breach point to investigate. Review every card that used it in the exposure window. Reissue the exposed cards and report the terminal to the acquirer.

sop.what: A trained scorecard ranks this card's transactions by model score and surfaces the highest-scoring one when it clears the model's alert threshold.
sop.why: This adds a learned signal trained on the population, scoring behavioral features (velocity, amount-vs-own-history, geographic jump, merchant and country novelty) with the seeded risk score excluded.
sop.brief: The trained model scored this transaction above its alert threshold. A score is a flag, not proof. Check the top factors in the trace. Compare against the account's normal pattern.
